system_description.narrative_title: Multipolar Flux: Energy shocks, finance stress, and tech–security decoupling
system_description.narrative_summary: The global order is an open, tightly coupled system in transitional flux: regional wars and Mideast disruptions are driving volatile energy flows that feed inflation and corporate stress, while sovereign bond markets — notably in Europe — are testing fiscal resilience. Simultaneously, strategic competition over technology and supply chains (China, Taiwan, rare earths, semiconductors) and US domestic politics (elections, executive interventions) are producing cross-border spillovers that reshape alliances, markets and crisis management. These processes interact nonlinearly, so shocks in one domain (oil, bonds, or tech) rapidly propagate through trade, finance and security networks.
system_description.scope: Interstate conflict and diplomacy; global energy and commodity flows; international finance and sovereign bond markets; strategic technology supply chains and export controls; major-power competition and proxy wars (Russia–Ukraine, US–Iran tensions); domestic political cycles with international spillovers.
system_description.super_system: The global political-economic system — a 21st-century, market-finance-driven international order in a multipolar transition (geopolitical, economic and technological layers).
adjacent_subsystems: Middle East energy–security subsystem (oil exports, regional conflict, Houthi/Iranian dynamics)
European financial-political subsystem (EU/eurozone sovereign debt, social unrest, governance)
Indo-Pacific tech–security subsystem (China–Taiwan tensions, semiconductor supply chains, rare earths)
US domestic politics & policy subsystem (elections, tariffs, executive actions affecting foreign policy)

variables.name: Middle East conflict and energy shocks
variables.description: The United States, Iran, Gulf states and regional militias are engaged in a volatile conflict that intermittently disrupts oil exports and is raising durable global energy risk premia.

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war and peace diplomacy
variables.description: Russia, Ukraine and Western mediators are locked in sustained combat punctuated by local ceasefires and renewed rounds of talks, shifting front-line dynamics, espionage and sabotage patterns.

variables.name: US–China strategic and technological competition
variables.description: The United States, China and their economic partners are contesting advanced tech, semiconductor supply chains, critical minerals and investment access, driving export controls, diversification and industrial reshoring.

variables.name: Western sovereign bond stress and capital-flows repricing
variables.description: Eurozone issuers (notably France), global investors and US Treasury markets are experiencing renewed sovereign-yield and credit-risk repricing that is reshaping policy space, safe-haven flows and financial stability calculations.

variables.name: Private space and satellite communications governance
variables.description: Governments (Western and regional) and dominant private space firms are disputing control, access and rules for satellite communications and space-based services, prompting efforts to diversify, nationalize and regulate critical constellations.
